You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure and the bug report indicate an OutOfMemoryError occurs when using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes. The test case uses the pattern "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!", which contains escaped single quotes and quoted strings.

From the constructor calls in ExtendedMessageFormat(java.lang.String, java.util.Map) and ExtendedMessageFormat(java.lang.String, Locale, java.util.Map), we see that the pattern is applied via applyPattern.

Examining applyPattern(String pattern), we observe the method processes the pattern character by character using a ParsePosition and handles quoted strings via appendQuotedString. When it encounters a quote (QUOTE), it calls appendQuotedString with escapingOn=true.

The appendQuotedString method handles quoted strings and escaped quotes by iterating through the pattern. It detects escaped quotes (two single quotes) and appends a single quote accordingly, advancing the position. If it encounters an unterminated quoted string, it throws an IllegalArgumentException.

The logic seems correct at first glance, but looking closer: If the pattern contains consecutive single quotes representing an escaped quote (like "it''s"), the method appendQuotedString appends one quote and increments the position past the second quote and continues. However, if for some reason the offset increments are off or the advancing in the main loop in applyPattern misaligns with the position updates in appendQuotedString, the loop might never progress past certain positions.

In particular, applyPattern uses a switch on the current char and advances the position mainly via next(pos) only in the default case. For the QUOTE case, appendQuotedString is called, which internally updates pos to correctly advance past the quoted string or escaped quote.

If appendQuotedString, due to the logic, does not correctly advance the ParsePosition after an escaped quote, the while loop in applyPattern will indefinitely process the same position without moving forward, causing an infinite loop and thus OutOfMemoryError.

This issue arises specifically when a custom format registry is provided (registry != null) because in that case, the code path with custom parsing and quoted string handling is exercised. The root cause is in appendQuotedString handling of escaped quotes combined with the main loop's position management in applyPattern, causing infinite looping over the same character.

Therefore, the bug is that appendQuotedString plus applyPattern incorrectly handle patterns with escaped quotes (double single quotes) and a custom registry, causing infinite looping and OutOfMemoryError.

This diagnosis aligns with the test pattern "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!" (contains escaped quotes 'it''s') and leads to the OutOfMemoryError described.

Similar recent bug reports do not relate to this pattern parsing issue, so they do not add additional insight here.

# Suggested fixes will be in the methods that handle parsing and quoted strings.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The OutOfMemoryError reported when using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and patterns containing single quotes arises from the handling of quoted strings and escaped quotes in the applyPattern and appendQuotedString methods. The test pattern "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!" contains escaped single quotes ('it''s'). The applyPattern method processes the pattern character by character, calling appendQuotedString when encountering quote characters. The appendQuotedString method is responsible for advancing the ParsePosition past quoted text, including handling escaped quotes (two consecutive single quotes). However, a flaw in appendQuotedString causes it to not correctly advance the ParsePosition in some cases with escaped quotes, leading to an infinite loop in applyPattern's main parsing loop (since the position is not incremented properly). This infinite loop results in OutOfMemoryError. This behavior only manifests when a custom format registry is provided, as this triggers the extended parsing logic in applyPattern. Overall, the interaction between applyPattern and appendQuotedString parsing logic mishandles escaped quotes, causing an endless loop and thus memory exhaustion for patterns containing such escaped quotes.

Suggested fix locations:
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String, java.text.ParsePosition, java.lang.StringBuffer, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
